perf.resNote: Of {total} fetched, {cached} never touched the wire (cache, service worker) · {blockers} blocked the first paint.
perf.resTaoNote: If every phase column is “—”, it is {other}, and that side did not send {header}.
perf.worstFrame: The latest frame: {worst} (finger blocked {blocking} · drawing {render}) — {n} late frames.
perf.unusedNote: Fetched but never drawn this time: {n} ({size}).
perf.budgetUnknown: None over — but {n} could not be measured
perf.budgetNotMeasured: Not measured: {list} — they are not counted as passing.
perf.noProbe: {file} must load before the shell ({shell}). Try building again ({cmd}) or refreshing. We will not invent numbers to show you.
perf.lead: KarmoLab’s own performance. It is measured in one place, the shell ({where}); this screen only reads. The numbers are {measured}, and what could not be measured is left as {dash}.
perf.noWidgets: No widget has been opened yet. Open a few tools and press {again} to fill this table.
perf.floorNote: The display floor of this environment is {floor} (the median of a click that does nothing). The painting column is coloured by {over} — the floor itself is time spent by the machine and the browser, not by our code.
perf.forcedLayout: A row marked {what} is code that read and wrote in turns, making the browser compute twice.
perf.unusedWhy: {onDemand} — it may be the next screen. The problem is {atBoot}: fetched without a press, and never used{count}.
perf.bundleTotal: {n} in all · gzip total {size} (nobody fetches them all — only what they press). This table is {cached}, so widgets nobody opened show up too. The 64KB limit and the regression ratchet are watched by {cmd} in CI.
perf.realNote: The last 14 days. Counted in buckets, so it is {bound} (“at most this”). Under 20 rounds gathered, it is still just numbers. No individual is kept — we only tally one into a bucket per day.
perf.clsNote: Movement right after a press (opening a tab and so on) is excluded — that is usually intended. The total counts only {window} (adding everything up would punish leaving it open longer).
perf.sampleNote: A row with fewer than 3 samples is {trust} — the same code doubles when the machine is busy. Rounds that cannot be trusted (hidden tabs, restored pages) are excluded from the start.
perf.trustNote: In the boots-by-build table such rows are marked {mark} as well.
perf.frameMeasuring: Measuring frames… {sec}s. {front} — send it to the back and the browser stops drawing, so the numbers lie.
perf.frameResult: The last {sec}s — average {fps} · worst 1% {low} · frames over 33ms {janks} (worst frame {worst}) · {frames} frames drawn.
perf.frameIdleNote: If fps sits near 60 on a screen left alone, it means {redraw}.
